fact: ITWeb Africa reports that amendments to the CBK Act brought non-deposit-taking digital lenders under Central Bank of Kenya supervision, requiring a licence before operating, with 281 digital credit providers licensed by September 2026.

Seven Kenyan regulators including the CBK issued a draft Financial Consumer Protection Framework for public consultation, applying to all financial service providers, their agents and digital channels, with comments due 28 April 2026.
The Central Bank of Kenya says the draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 aims to secure financial stability through risk management, consumer and data protection.
Business Daily reports Competition Authority of Kenya data showing borrower complaints about digital lenders rose to 355 cases in the year to June 2025 from 67 the year before.
Business Daily reports the Competition Authority of Kenya received 355 complaints from borrowers about digital lenders' hidden charges, changed terms and asset seizure in the year to June 2025.
